content.overview: Light measurements should be integrated with time and crop context. PPFD describes photon flux at an instant/location, photoperiod describes light duration, and DLI describes accumulated photosynthetic photons over a day. These metrics are related but not interchangeable.

vocabulary.definition: Photosynthetic photon flux density, commonly expressed as micromoles of photons per square meter per second.
The duration of the light period within a 24-hour cycle.
The daily accumulated amount of photosynthetically active photons received per unit area, expressed as moles per square meter per day.

sections.title: Instantaneous intensity is not daily dose
sections.body: A single PPFD measurement cannot describe daily photon exposure without time information. DLI integrates PPFD across the photoperiod and any changing light conditions.

sections.title: Measure where the crop receives light
sections.body: Canopy geometry, fixture spacing, shading and room structure create spatial light differences. Measurement grids are stronger than a single center reading when evaluating uniformity.

sections.title: Light changes environmental load and crop response
sections.body: Lighting adds heat and changes plant transpiration and water demand. Evaluate light alongside temperature, humidity, airflow and root-zone response instead of treating it as an isolated variable.

workedExamples: Two rooms can have the same average PPFD but different DLI if their photoperiods differ; conversely, similar DLI can be delivered through different intensity-duration combinations with different crop/environment implications.
commonMistakes: Using lux in place of a plant-relevant photon measurement without a justified conversion/context.
Treating one center-canopy PPFD value as a uniformity map.
Copying DLI targets from another species or facility as a cannabis universal.
content.practicalApplication: Create a canopy PPFD grid, compute an illustrative DLI from a stable PPFD and photoperiod, then state the limitations of that calculation when intensity varies through the day.
content.summary: PPFD, photoperiod and DLI answer different light questions. Specialist interpretation requires both measurement geometry and crop/environment context.
